An '''alta-wave calibration device''' was a type of calibration device with a flat [[Color/Legends|gray]] base and a hooked arm on a stand at one end of the base.<ref name="Inside" /> When the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his allies visited the [[Wald's Parts|junkshop]] owned by the [[Junk dealer/Legends|junk dealer]] [[Watto/Legends|Watto]] in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in search of a [[T-14 hyperdrive generator/Legends|T-14 hyperdrive generator]]<ref name="Inside" /> in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|I}}, as depicted in ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'', to [[32 BBY]].</ref> an illegal alta-wave calibration device was sat by the store's back door.<ref name="Inside" />

==Behind the scenes==
An alta-wave calibration device was first mentioned in the [[2000]] reference book ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'', which was written by [[Kristin Lund]] and illustrated by [[Richard Chasemore]] and [[Hans Jenssen]]. The illustration of Watto's junkshop from that book,<ref name="Inside">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]''</ref> including the alta-wave calibration device, then appeared as an area where players would search out specific items in the<ref name="Spy">{{SWArchive|url=play/online-games/galactic-spy|text=''Star Wars Galactic Spy''|int=Star Wars Galactic Spy}}</ref> [[2012]]<ref name="SpyDate">{{SW|url=news/starwars-com-weekly-roundup-september-28-2012|text=StarWars.com Weekly Roundup: September 28, 2012}}</ref> non-[[canon]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Galactic Spy]]''.<ref name="Spy" />
